subject: Variational number of samples + on non-convergence where do samples come from?

messages.author: fb40a65bd21dcf6f
messages.subject: Variational number of samples + on non-convergence where do samples come from?
parts:
When I ask for 200 samples in the variational command line I get 201 samples back with the first looking like an outlier. Can anyone let me know where this extra sample is coming from? Am I misinterpreting the output? My command line looks like:

../inst/Stan/MTKL variational output_samples=200 tol_rel_obj=0.01 iter=3500 data file=MTKL_data.R

Also when I reach the maximum iterations without convergence, do the samples come from the final iteration or the one with best ELBO?

Thanks,
John.

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Variational number of samples + on non-convergence where do samples come from?
parts:
hi john,

the first “sample" is the mean set of parameters outputted by the variational distribution. it is not meant to be used as a sample but as a quick summary statistic of the distribution. you can find more in the manual in cmdstan—hope that helps

dustin

should match the one output for MCMC if at all possible.

Would it be possible to take that summary of means and write it
out as a comment? Or in a separate output file?

Going forward, we're going to split the outputs in Stan 3 (if
I get my way) so that we don't try to overload CSV notation with
out-of-encoding comment information that needs to be parsed, which
is too hard to deal with other than with our own I/O tools (which
themselves become hard to maintain).

messages.author: 453ddfeccaf29bbb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Variational number of samples + on non-convergence where do samples come from?
parts:
hi john,

i would vote against this for two reasons: 1) the ELBO really should
be increasing throughout the optimization and 2) our evaluation of the
ELBO itself is stochastic (noisy). therefore, taking samples from the
iteration with the best ELBO may not be reliable at all.

cheers
alp

On Tue, Nov 3, 2015 at 4:40 AM, John Reid <johnba...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Alp,
> Does it make more sense to take them from the iteration with the best ELBO?
> Cheers, John.
